page.layout: One printed page, framed by an ornamental border. Running text in one column, full width inside the border. No marginal notes. Page number and running head at the top.

main_text.p: ctura loco salis fusilis naturæ, suo ipsius sale contenta est, & extribus auri præsertim Philosophici principiis resolutis, depuratis, & conjunctis prodit, ut sub finem dicemus.

Quarta Tinctura secundum Basilii sententiam est Tinctura Veneris & Martis, in unum videlicet conflatorum, hoc est, ex eorum vitrioli albo & rubenti spiritu, qui est Mercurius & Sulphur amborum, unà cum eorundem fixo sale, unde hæc tinctura paratur: licet sine Sole vulgari, cum quo illa est incorporanda, non perficiatur; siquidem prius cum eo figenda est, quemadmodum testatur Basilius in lib. de Naturalibus & Supernaturalib⁹ rebus cap. 2. pag. 28. his ipsis verbis: Quando enim (inquit) Tinctura Solis

page.notes: The catchword "lis" is written at the right below the last line. The final line is partly italic. The text has a few printed irregularities (e.g. "Supernaturalib⁹" with superscript 9, and the spacing "sineSole", "eaSo-") left as printed. Some words in the upper-left border are hard to read but they are ornament, not text.
